title: Page Through a Moving List
description: New orders arrive while a client pages newest-first. Offset pages repeat rows, and several orders share a creation timestamp. Which change addresses shifting offsets without promising a snapshot?

options.text: Keep offsets but increase the page size.
options.explanation: Larger pages reduce request count, not the shifting positions caused by inserts before the next offset.

options.text: Use created_at alone as the cursor.
options.explanation: Tied timestamps leave no unique boundary; rows sharing that timestamp can be skipped or repeated.

options.text: Sort each page independently after applying its offset.
options.explanation: Sorting after selecting a shifting slice cannot restore a stable boundary between pages.

options.text: Use an opaque (created_at, id) cursor with fixed filters.
options.explanation: A unique tie-breaker gives keyset pagination a stable boundary. Index the sort columns; updates still require a separate snapshot guarantee if one is needed.
